_cell_header.carries: Magnitude versus rank. Does the model ESTIMATE a distance between priority numbers, or just LOOK UP which one is higher?
_cell_header.the_test: Under a magnitude reading, 88 against 61 should separate more than 62 against 61, even though the order is identical. Under a lookup reading the two should behave the same. This is the cleanest available test of the two accounts, and it gives capacity for declared tiers — the number deployments actually ask for.
_cell_header.held_fixed: Both spans use the SAME transport (user) and the SAME displayed provenance (repository configuration). Only the declared rank differs. Declared rank is a covariate attached to a span that already has a transport and a provenance — never a sixth source, because one extra category could not identify a distance coefficient.
_cell_header.who_declares_the_rule: The operator's system message states the precedence rule. The ranks themselves sit inside repo-config spans, so no span writes its own authority. The rule direction is reversed in tier-09 on purpose.
_cell_header.notation_control: tier-10 carries the same encoding as tier-05 in a different tag format. Meaning-preserving format changes alone can move accuracy substantially, so a published 'notation effect' may be a format effect rather than an authority effect. Without this control we could not tell.
